name: Spirit
first: First of the Mars Exploration Rover twins; longest-lived rover until passed by Curiosity
description: Spirit (MER-A) bounced 28 times across the floor of Gusev Crater on 2004-01-04 and rolled to a stop 250 m from its first impact. Designed for a 90-sol primary mission, it would survive 2,210 sols. Drove 7.7 km across Gusev's plains, climbed the Columbia Hills, and uncovered hematite-bearing rocks that signalled persistent ancient water. In 2009-04 a wheel broke through a sulphate crust at "Troy" and Spirit ground to a halt in soft soil; the team converted it to a stationary platform. Final transmission 2010-03-22; mission declared ended 2011-05-25. Twinned with Opportunity, which landed three weeks later on the opposite side of Mars.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Delta II 7925 from Cape Canaveral LC-17A.

events.label: EDL
events.note: Heat shield, parachute, retro-rockets, airbags — 6 minutes of hell into Gusev Crater.

events.label: TOUCHDOWN
events.note: Bounced 28 times. Rolled to rest at 14.57°S, 175.47°E.

events.label: STUCK AT TROY
events.note: Wheel breaks through sulphate crust; rover bogs down in soft soil. 2009-04.
